---
title: "The Complete Concept Map"
subtitle: "Every idea in machine learning for biology, labeled by what kind of thing it is"
page-layout: full
---

Machine learning terms get confusing because they belong to **different kinds of categories** that are usually listed together. This page sorts them. The colors show what kind of thing each idea is:

| Color | Kind of thing | The question it answers | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| <span style="background:#FDE2E0;border:2px solid #C0392B;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px">red</span> | **Paradigm** | What does my training data look like? | Supervised |
| <span style="background:#FCEBD9;border:2px dashed #D35400;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px">orange, dashed</span> | **Hybrid paradigm** | A mix of two paradigms | Self-supervised |
| <span style="background:#E3EDFB;border:2px solid #1B4CA8;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px">blue</span> | **Task** | What kind of answer do I want? | Classification |
| <span style="background:#E3F3EC;border:2px solid #0E6B58;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px">green</span> | **Method / model family** | What machine produces the answer? | Random forest |
| <span style="background:#FFF6D6;border:2px solid #B7950B;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px">yellow</span> | **Pipeline step** | A choice every project makes | Loss function |
| <span style="background:#FFFFFF;border:2px solid #999;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px">white</span> | **Option** | One possible answer to a pipeline choice | Ridge (L2) |
| <span style="background:#F1E6F7;border:2px solid #7D3C98;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px">purple</span> | **Strategy / approach** | A way of working that cuts across paradigms | Transfer learning |
| <span style="background:#EEEEEE;border:2px solid #555;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px">grey</span> | **Math tool** | The math underneath | Hessian |

## Map 1: Paradigms → Tasks → Methods

*Read left to right: what your data looks like → what you want to predict or find → the model families that can do it. Dashed lines mark hybrids.*

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  ML(["Machine learning"])

  ML --> SUP["<b>Supervised</b><br/>inputs + answers"]
  ML --> UNS["<b>Unsupervised</b><br/>inputs only"]
  ML --> RL["<b>Reinforcement</b><br/>actions + rewards"]
  SUP -.-> SEMI["<b>Semi-supervised</b><br/>few answers + many unlabeled"]
  UNS -.-> SEMI
  SUP -.-> SELF["<b>Self-supervised</b><br/>answers made from the input itself"]
  UNS -.-> SELF
  SUP -.-> WEAK["<b>Weakly supervised</b><br/>coarse or noisy answers"]

  SUP --> REG["Regression<br/><i>y is a number</i><br/>disease progression"]
  SUP --> CLS["Classification<br/><i>y is a category</i>"]
  CLS --> BIN["Binary<br/>malignant vs benign"]
  CLS --> MCL["Multiclass<br/>one of 10 cell types"]
  CLS --> MLB["Multilabel<br/>protein with several functions"]
  SUP --> SURV["Time-to-event / survival<br/>time to relapse, some not yet observed"]
  SUP --> SEQL["Per-position labeling<br/>exon vs intron at each base"]
  SUP --> STRP["Structured prediction<br/>a whole 3D protein structure"]

  REG --> SMF["Supervised model families<br/><i>most do regression AND classification</i>"]
  CLS --> SMF
  SMF --> LIN["Linear models<br/>linear and logistic regression, GLMs"]
  SMF --> KNN["k-nearest neighbors"]
  SMF --> NBY["Naive Bayes"]
  SMF --> SVM["Support vector machines"]
  SMF --> GPR["Gaussian processes"]
  SMF --> TREE["Decision trees"]
  TREE --> ENS["Tree ensembles<br/>random forest, gradient boosting"]
  SMF --> NN["Neural networks"]
  NN --> MLP["MLP / fully connected<br/>tabular data"]
  NN --> CNN["CNN<br/>DNA motifs, microscopy images"]
  NN --> RNN["RNN / LSTM<br/>sequences, time series"]
  NN --> TRF["Transformer<br/>protein sequences, AlphaFold"]
  NN --> GNN["Graph neural network<br/>molecules, interaction networks"]
  SURV --> COX["Cox proportional hazards<br/>random survival forests"]
  SEQL --> HMM["Hidden Markov models<br/>gene finding, protein families"]
  STRP --> TRF

  UNS --> CLU["Clustering<br/>cell types, strains"]
  UNS --> DRD["Dimensionality reduction<br/>20,000 genes to a few axes"]
  UNS --> DEN["Density estimation and generative<br/>model the data, make new samples"]
  UNS --> ANO["Anomaly detection<br/>contaminated samples, rare cells"]
  CLU --> KMN["k-means"]
  CLU --> HCL["Hierarchical clustering"]
  CLU --> GMM["Gaussian mixture models"]
  CLU --> DBS["DBSCAN"]
  CLU --> LEI["Leiden / Louvain graph clustering<br/>standard in single-cell"]
  DRD --> PCA["PCA<br/>linear"]
  DRD --> NMF["NMF, ICA, factor analysis"]
  DRD --> UMP["t-SNE / UMAP<br/>nonlinear, for visualization"]
  DRD --> AEN["Autoencoders"]
  DEN --> GMM
  DEN --> KDE["Kernel density estimation"]
  DEN --> VAE["VAEs<br/>scVI for single-cell"]
  DEN --> DIF["Diffusion models<br/>protein design"]
  DEN --> GAN["GANs"]
  DEN --> HMM
  ANO --> ISO["Isolation forest"]
  ANO --> AEN

  SELF --> MSK["Masked prediction<br/>hide amino acids: ESM protein LMs"]
  SELF --> NXT["Next-token prediction<br/>generate protein sequences"]
  SELF --> CON["Contrastive learning<br/>two views of one cell should match"]
  SEMI --> PSL["Pseudo-labeling / self-training"]
  SEMI --> LPR["Label propagation"]
  WEAK --> MIL["Multiple-instance learning<br/>slide-level diagnosis, unlabeled patches"]
  RL --> QLR["Value-based: Q-learning"]
  RL --> PGR["Policy gradient"]
  RL --> BND["Bandits<br/>which experiment to run next"]

  classDef paradigm fill:#FDE2E0,stroke:#C0392B,stroke-width:2px,color:#2C2C2A
  classDef hybrid fill:#FCEBD9,stroke:#D35400,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:6 4,color:#2C2C2A
  classDef task fill:#E3EDFB,stroke:#1B4CA8,stroke-width:2px,color:#2C2C2A
  classDef method fill:#E3F3EC,stroke:#0E6B58,stroke-width:2px,color:#2C2C2A
  classDef root fill:#2C2C2A,stroke:#2C2C2A,color:#FFFFFF
  class ML root
  class SUP,UNS,RL paradigm
  class SEMI,SELF,WEAK hybrid
  class REG,CLS,BIN,MCL,MLB,SURV,SEQL,STRP,CLU,DRD,DEN,ANO,MSK,NXT,CON task
  class SMF,LIN,KNN,NBY,SVM,GPR,TREE,ENS,NN,MLP,CNN,RNN,TRF,GNN,COX,HMM,KMN,HCL,GMM,DBS,LEI,PCA,NMF,UMP,AEN,KDE,VAE,DIF,GAN,ISO,PSL,LPR,MIL,QLR,PGR,BND method
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Why some methods appear in several places:** a method is a tool, not a category. **PCA** is a standalone unsupervised method, but it is *also* used as a preprocessing step inside supervised pipelines (see Map 2). **HMMs** label sequences and also model densities. **Autoencoders** reduce dimensions and also detect anomalies.
:::

## Map 2: The pipeline: choices every project makes

*Whatever paradigm and model you choose, you walk through these steps. Yellow = the step; white = the options at that step.*

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph S0["0 · Question and data"]
    direction TB
    Q1["What is one sample? What is y?"]
    Q2["How many samples n vs features p?"]
  end
  subgraph S1["1 · Split the data FIRST"]
    direction TB
    SP1["Train / validation / test"]
    SP2["k-fold cross-validation"]
    SP3["Leakage: never let test data touch training"]
  end
  subgraph S2["2 · Preprocessing"]
    direction TB
    P1["Center / standardize features"]
    P2["Log-transform counts"]
    P3["Normalize library size, RNA-seq"]
    P4["Batch-effect correction"]
    P5["Impute missing values"]
    P6["One-hot encode categories"]
    P7["Feature selection"]
    P8["PCA as preprocessing"]
  end
  subgraph S3["3 · Model family"]
    direction TB
    M1["See Map 1"]
    M2["Hyperparameters: set by you, not learned"]
  end
  subgraph S4["4 · Loss function"]
    direction TB
    L1["MSE: Gaussian noise"]
    L2["MAE / Huber: outliers"]
    L3["Binary cross-entropy"]
    L4["Categorical cross-entropy"]
    L5["Hinge: SVMs"]
    L6["Poisson / negative binomial: count data"]
    L7["Cox partial likelihood: survival"]
    L8["Reconstruction + KL: VAEs"]
    L9["Contrastive loss"]
  end
  subgraph S5["5 · Regularization: fight overfitting"]
    direction TB
    R1["Ridge, L2"]
    R2["Lasso, L1: sparse"]
    R3["Elastic net, L1 + L2"]
    R4["Dropout"]
    R5["Early stopping"]
    R6["Data augmentation"]
    R7["Tree depth limits / pruning"]
  end
  subgraph S6["6 · Optimizer: how to minimize the loss"]
    direction TB
    O1["Closed form: normal equation"]
    O2["Full-batch gradient descent"]
    O3["Stochastic gradient descent, 1 sample"]
    O4["Mini-batch gradient descent"]
    O5["Momentum / Adam"]
    O6["Newton's method: uses the Hessian"]
    O7["Coordinate descent: lasso"]
    O8["EM algorithm: GMMs, HMMs"]
    O9["Greedy splitting: trees"]
  end
  subgraph S7["7 · Evaluation"]
    direction TB
    E1["Regression: MSE, R²"]
    E2["Classification: accuracy, precision, recall, ROC-AUC, confusion matrix"]
    E3["Clustering: silhouette, agreement with known labels"]
    E4["Calibration: are probabilities honest?"]
    E5["Diagnose: overfitting vs underfitting, bias-variance trade-off"]
    E6["Tune hyperparameters on validation data"]
  end
  subgraph S8["8 · Interpretation and inference"]
    direction TB
    I1["Feature importance / SHAP"]
    I2["Predict new samples, same preprocessing"]
    I3["Extrapolation warnings"]
  end
  S0 --> S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5 --> S6 --> S7 --> S8
  S7 -. "not good enough? go back" .-> S2

  classDef option fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#999999,color:#2C2C2A
  class Q1,Q2,SP1,SP2,SP3,P1,P2,P3,P4,P5,P6,P7,P8,M1,M2,L1,L2,L3,L4,L5,L6,L7,L8,L9,R1,R2,R3,R4,R5,R6,R7,O1,O2,O3,O4,O5,O6,O7,O8,O9,E1,E2,E3,E4,E5,E6,I1,I2,I3 option
  style S0 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
  style S1 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
  style S2 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
  style S3 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
  style S4 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
  style S5 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
  style S6 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
  style S7 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
  style S8 fill:#FFF6D6,stroke:#B7950B,stroke-width:2px
```

## Map 3: Strategies and approaches that cut across everything

*These are not paradigms or models. They are ways of working that can be combined with almost any of them.*

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph A1["Statistical approach: how you treat the unknown parameters"]
    direction TB
    F1["Frequentist / MLE<br/>find the single best w"]
    B1["Bayesian<br/>prior × likelihood → posterior over w"]
    MAP["MAP estimate<br/>the peak of the posterior"]
    B1 --> MAP
    MAP --> RID["Ridge = MAP with a Gaussian prior<br/>Lasso = MAP with a Laplace prior"]
  end
  subgraph A2["Learning strategies"]
    direction TB
    T1["Transfer learning and fine-tuning<br/>pretrain big, adapt to your small dataset"]
    T2["Active learning<br/>model picks the next experiment"]
    T3["Online learning<br/>update as new data streams in"]
    T4["Multi-task learning<br/>one model, several related outputs"]
    T5["Ensembling<br/>bagging, boosting, stacking"]
    T6["Federated learning<br/>train across hospitals without sharing data"]
  end
  subgraph A3["Model properties"]
    direction TB
    D1["Discriminative: models p(y given x)<br/>logistic regression, most neural nets"]
    D2["Generative: models p(x, y) or p(x)<br/>naive Bayes, HMMs, VAEs, diffusion"]
    D3["Parametric: fixed number of parameters<br/>linear models, neural nets"]
    D4["Non-parametric: grows with the data<br/>k-NN, Gaussian processes, trees"]
  end

  classDef strategy fill:#F1E6F7,stroke:#7D3C98,stroke-width:2px,color:#2C2C2A
  class F1,B1,MAP,RID,T1,T2,T3,T4,T5,T6,D1,D2,D3,D4 strategy
  style A1 fill:#FAFAF8,stroke:#BBBBBB
  style A2 fill:#FAFAF8,stroke:#BBBBBB
  style A3 fill:#FAFAF8,stroke:#BBBBBB
```

  classDef math fill:#EEEEEE,stroke:#555555,stroke-width:2px,color:#2C2C2A
